Navigation and permissions

Every page keeps institution, active course/term and current role clear. Academic content must retain its context when opened from search, calendar or activity. Page IDs are stable planning keys; URL patterns are proposed implementation guidance.

Shells

Access shell (W01-W04): Whiteboard identity, institution chooser/identity handoff, status/recovery and help. No signed-in course navigation before a valid sample identity/context exists. The institution owns credentials; Whiteboard does not draw a fake institutional password box.

Global shell (W05-W12): Today, Courses, Calendar, Activity and Tools in the primary sidebar. Top bar contains search, account, active role/context and help. Student home leads with next academic work; instructor home leads with course preparation/grading/release exceptions; TA home leads with assigned work and its deadline. Course roles come from enrollments, not an unrestricted production role switch.

Student course shell (W14-W34): Course breadcrumb and term, Overview, Modules, Coursework, Calendar, Announcements, Discussions, Grades and Groups. Syllabus is a visible overview link. Tools can be reached with a course filter. Assignment feedback and receipts remain nested under their assessment. Group access appears only where enrolled; no private course messaging tab.

Staff course shell (W35-W60): Course breadcrumb and term, Builder, Assessments, Grading, Gradebook, People, Groups, Calendar, Announcements, Discussions and Settings. Files, Rubrics, Question bank, Allowances, Grading allocations, Insights and Copy/Import appear as grouped course tools rather than an unstructured 26-item sidebar. A TA sees only allowed entries and informative read-only views. A deep URL still requires a permission check.

System template (W13): Distinct session-expired, access-denied, not-found, maintenance and service-error variants with safe navigation. Hide private record metadata on unauthorized pages. A 404 response must not confirm that another student's submission exists.

Optional achievements/assistant entries are absent by default. If enabled later, keep their dependency and course-policy rules explicit. No admin/campus navigation should appear just because the historical prototype includes it.

This is a proposed default matrix for HTML review. Real authorization must later be enforced server-side; disabled buttons, hidden menus and client-side role switches do not secure production data.

Navigation rules

  • Global links retain the selected term/filter. Course links preserve courseId; assessment links preserve assignment/quiz and attempt IDs. Browser Back returns to the previous list/query/date and scroll position when feasible.
  • Course switcher lists only accessible offerings. If an equivalent destination exists in another course, navigate there; otherwise use that course's overview and announce the context change. Never carry a learner/attempt ID into an unrelated course.
  • On role change, clear sensitive rendered data and reload permitted records. Expired TA access blocks mutation immediately and offers an instructor contact/recovery path; saved attributed grading remains intact.
  • Student preview is conspicuous and reversible. It uses the publication/availability rules of a real student and cannot submit, mark completion, trigger reminders or release results.
  • Unsaved work prompts Save draft / Discard / Keep editing where saving is supported. An unavailable network cannot produce “Saved to course.” Maintain the distinction between local draft, queued work and accepted record.
  • Direct links into archived courses show read-only context and current access conditions. Membership/retention checks apply even if the user remembers an old URL.
  • Use ordinary links for navigation. Preserve modified clicks, copy-link and browser history. Use buttons for actions. Sort/filter controls retain query state; state-demo controls remain outside product UI.
  • Calendar source colors supplement text. Private events, course events, student due dates and staff grading targets are separately toggleable sources. Hiding a source never changes its records.

Counting and legacy mapping

The new W inventory deliberately makes previously omitted academic workflows explicit. W24 is a real learner course gradebook; W52 is policy configuration; W47 is group management; W57 supplies TA grading deadlines. They are not satisfied by a generic menu label or a historical S19 staff table. data/legacy-crosswalk.json maps every included S/P academic destination to this proposal. Historical IDs and original accepted tracker remain unchanged.
